ORTHOPEDIC CONSULTATION NOTE
Patient: Synthetic Patient A (P001)
Date of Service: 2026-04-02

History of Present Illness:
Recreational soccer player presents after a non-contact pivoting injury to the left knee. Reports immediate swelling and a sensation of the knee giving way when changing direction.

Physical Examination:
Left knee with moderate effusion. Lachman test positive with a soft endpoint. Anterior drawer positive. McMurray negative. Flexion limited by pain and guarding.

Assessment:
Suspected left anterior cruciate ligament tear.

Plan:
Obtain MRI of the left knee to confirm. Recommend a 12 week course of physical therapy before any consideration of operative management. Will prescribe naproxen 500 mg twice daily.

MRI LEFT KNEE WITHOUT CONTRAST
Accession: MR-2026-0720-114
Date of Service: 2026-07-20
Indication: Left knee instability following a pivoting injury.

FINDINGS:
Anterior cruciate ligament: Complete full-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament at the femoral attachment, with fiber discontinuity and adjacent marrow edema.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Intact.
Menisci: No meniscal tear identified.
Cartilage: No focal chondral defect.

IMPRESSION:
1. Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Small joint effusion.

PHYSICAL THERAPY PROGRESS NOTE
Patient: Synthetic Patient A (P001)
Date of Service: 2026-09-10
Referring Provider: Orthopedic Surgery

Plan of Care: Supervised rehabilitation for a left knee ligamentous injury.
Attendance: 16 of 16 scheduled visits completed.
Home exercise program reviewed and updated at each visit.

--- Page 2 ---
Interim Summary:
The patient has completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy, attending twice weekly since 2026-07-16.
Strength testing improved to 4+/5 on the involved side.
Despite completion of the full course, the patient continues to report persistent instability of the left knee with pivoting and with descending stairs.
Functional testing was deferred because of ongoing giving way episodes.

MEDICATION AND CONSERVATIVE CARE HISTORY
Patient: Synthetic Patient A (P001)
Date of Service: 2026-09-10

Naproxen 500 mg twice daily was taken for 6 weeks beginning 2026-04-05, with partial relief of pain and no improvement in mechanical symptoms.
Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed was subsequently trialed.
No opioid analgesics were prescribed.
Bracing: Hinged knee brace issued 2026-04-10 and worn during activity.
